issues.title: error C2872: 'std': ambiguous symbol when compiling `csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h`
issues.author: JulianKnodt
issues.body:
I've been trying to compile simple-knn which is a submodule of gaussian splatting, and have been hitting a compile bug inside of pytorch.

When running `pip install submodules/simple-knn` (https://gitlab.inria.fr/bkerbl/simple-knn.git), I am running into a compile error in the following file:

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/3ac92f2d1330d75799d3ee6cfe8e509615fb1854/torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h#L1142

I don't think it matters the specific thing I'm trying to compile, but for reproducibility thought it may be useful.

The error is

```
spatial.cu
      tmpxft_0000106c_00000000-7_spatial.cudafe1.cpp
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1136): error C2872: 'std': ambiguous symbol
      C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Community/VC/Tools/MSVC/14.50.35717/include\valarray(20): note: could be 'std'
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1136): note: or       'std'
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1136): note: the template instantiation context (the oldest one
      first) is
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1183): note: see reference to class template instantiation
      'torch::dynamo::autograd::IValuePacker<__int64>' being compiled
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1110): note: while compiling class template member function
      'c10::TypePtr torch::dynamo::autograd::IValuePacker<__int64>::packed_type(void)'
      C:/Users/Julian/Desktop/projects/python/gaussian-splatting/.venv/Lib/site-packages/torch/include\torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1183): note: see the first reference to
      'torch::dynamo::autograd::IValuePacker<__int64>::packed_type' in 'torch::dynamo::autograd::IValuePacker<unsigned __int64>::packed_type'
      ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

If I delete the line with `std::string`, or change `std::string` to another type without the `::std` or `std` prefix, the compile error goes away. In this case, I think just deleting is fine because these are compile time checks and if this code was actually being hit it would fail compilation. I don't know why I'm hitting this where others aren't (it's on a fresh install of windows and with a more recent possibly unsupported version of visual studios), but thought it was worth pointing it out.


cc @peterjc123 @mszhanyi @skyline75489 @nbcsm @iremyux @Blackhex @chauhang @penguinwu @xmfan @aditvenk

comments.author: JulianKnodt
comments.body:
My guess/understanding at this point is that when this template is instantiated somewhere by nvcc, at that point the namespace has been polluted with `std`, and that conflicts with the usage of `std` from the header file.

As an experiment, I tried:
- replacing `std::string` with just string, then this fails to compile.
- replacing `std::string` with `int32_t`, this compiles fine.
- replacing `std::string` with `std::int32_t`, this fails to compile.
I would imagine that std::is_same works fine since it's also instantiated outside of the context which pollutes the namespace (I'm not positive about this but it would make sense)

Other comments on this issue that I saw also note that it's fine if passing additional flags (I think `-Dpermissive` or something like it), since both `std` are the same (I imagine), but are introduced twice.

comments.author: Sahil170595
comments.body:
I reproduced this on a fresh setup and validated a fix end to end. Happy to submit the PR per @zou3519's earlier offer to test, unless @guilhermeleobas is still working on it.

**Repro (vanilla flags, no special config):** MSVC 14.42.34433 (cl 19.42.34444), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), torch 2.11.0+cu128, Python 3.13, Windows 11. Minimal extension: a `.cu` containing only `#include <torch/extension.h>` plus a trivial kernel, built via `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load()`. Result:

```
torch/csrc/dynamo/compiled_autograd.h(1143): error C2872: 'std': ambiguous symbol
  note: could be 'std' (valarray(20))
  note: the template instantiation context is ... IValuePacker<__int64>::packed_type
```

(line 1143 in the torch 2.11.0 release headers; the same branch is at line 1145 on current main)

**Why the existing carve-out never fires** (measured with a macro probe compiled under the same nvcc flags, host and device passes):

| macro | device pass | host pass |
|---|---|---|
| `_WIN32` | defined | defined |
| `__CUDACC__` | defined | defined |
| `USE_CUDA` | undefined | undefined |
| `USE_ROCM` | undefined | undefined |

`USE_CUDA` / `USE_ROCM` are libtorch build-config defines that downstream extension builds never set, so `#if defined(_WIN32) && (defined(USE_CUDA) || defined(USE_ROCM))` is false for every Windows CUDA extension build and the if-constexpr chain compiles under nvcc. (Downstream projects have been working around exactly this, e.g. by manually passing `-DUSE_CUDA` to their extension builds.)

**Fix validated on the failing box** (patched the installed header, re-ran the identical build):

1. Primary: add an explicit `IValuePacker<std::string>` specialization (mirroring the existing `size_t` and `std::vector<at::SymInt>` specializations) and drop the `else if constexpr (::std::is_same_v<T, ::std::string>)` branch from the primary-template chain. That branch is the only one in the chain whose right-hand type lives in namespace `std`, and it trips C2872 for every instantiation of the chain, which matches @JulianKnodt's earlier observation that altering that exact line unblocks the build. Semantically identical on all platforms; strings still pack as `at::StringType`. Builds clean, verified.
2. Also verified as a diagnostic: extending the guard with `|| defined(__CUDACC__)` fixes this config too. I would not ship that as the fix, since it routes extension TUs into the not-implemented carve-out (masking capability) and is macro-dependent, but it corroborates the mechanism.

If that shape sounds right I will put up the PR with the failing/passing logs and the macro table. cc @malfet @xmfan

comments.author: woct0rdho
woct0rdho
comments.body:
Update: When compiling with CUDA 13.2, we need
```python3
if os.name == "nt":
    NVCC_FLAGS += [
        "-Xcompiler=/Zc:preprocessor",
        "-D_WIN32=1",
        "-DUSE_CUDA=1",
    ]
```
Otherwise the non-standard preprocessor in MSVC called by nvcc will have trouble with `std`.

By the way, if we see
```python3
ABI = 1 if torch._C._GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI else 0
CXX_FLAGS += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
NVCC_FLAGS_COMMON += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
```
we need to replace with
```python3
if os.name != "nt":
    ABI = 1 if torch._C._GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI else 0
    CXX_FLAGS += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
    NVCC_FLAGS_COMMON += [f"-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI={ABI}"]
```
Because CXX11 ABI does not make sense on Windows, and it seems to cause nvcc going into some wrong codepath.

This issue still exists as of torch 2.12.0 . It's not strictly a bug of torch, but non-standard default behavior of MSVC, and we need the workaround anyway.

comments.author: malfet
comments.body:
> Reproduced on MSVC 14.42

@Sahil170595 I'm not very fluent in MSVC version numbers, but 14.42 seems to be coming from VS 2022. Any reason why you must use such an old compiler? VC++ is full of bugs, and I don't think PyTorch should strive to be compilable with every buggy version one can find

comments.author: Sahil170595
comments.body:
No attachment to 14.42, it is just what `vcvars64` picked. The version dependence is testable though, so I tested it. The same one-line repro (details in the PR) fires identically on every MSVC line I can find a data point for:

| MSVC toolset | cl | ships with | source | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14.42.34433 | 19.42 | VS 2022 17.12 | my box | C2872 |
| 14.43.34808 | 19.43 | VS 2022 17.13 | this issue's original traceback above | C2872 |
| 14.44.35217 | 19.44 | VS 2022 17.14, current | my box, just verified | C2872 |
| 14.50.35717 | 19.50 | VS 18 Community | #173232's traceback | C2872 |

So it does not look like an old-compiler artifact: the current VS 2022 toolset and the newest VS 18 toolset both hit it.

One more constraint on the "use a newer compiler" path: CUDA 13.0's `crt/host_config.h` hard-errors on `_MSC_VER >= 1950`, so VS 2022 toolsets (14.2x to 14.4x) are the newest host compilers nvcc officially supports there (newer toolkits may raise the ceiling), and per #173232 the 14.50 toolset reproduces anyway.

Agreed that PyTorch should not chase every buggy MSVC. The reason I would still fix this one: it fires on all currently supported host compilers for the default `torch.utils.cpp_extension` path, and the fix is a semantics-preserving rearrangement rather than a compiler workaround: the construct just moves out of the always-instantiated template path.

issues.title: rms_norm autocast fp32 policy (2.12) materializes standalone cast kernels under torch.compile when dtypes already match. Peak-memory and throughput regression for bf16 models
issues.author: abhishek-patnia-nu
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

torch 2.12 registered `rms_norm` under autocast's `fp32` cast policy ([#174824](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174824)). The policy applies unconditionally, including when input and weight are already both bf16. On torch 2.11 the op had no autocast registration, so in this configuration it ran bf16-in/bf16-out and autocast played no role.

```python
# torch 2.12.1, bf16 input AND bf16 weight:
with torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    y = norm(x_bf16)     # y.dtype == torch.float32  <- promoted regardless
with torch.autocast('cuda', enabled=False):
    y = norm(x_bf16)     # y.dtype == torch.bfloat16
```

The promotion inserts an fp32 upcast of the activation before every norm and leaves an fp32 output
that is downcast by the next `lower_precision_fp` op. Under `torch.compile`, these casts are graph
nodes with multiple consumers (the promoted input feeds both the statistic reduction and the
elementwise normalize). Some fuse into the generated norm kernels, but a large fraction are emitted
as standalone `triton_poi_fused__to_copy*` kernels, each writing a full-size buffer — a full fp32
copy of the activation per cast.

The promotion also provides no numerical benefit in this configuration: `rms_norm` upcasts
internally regardless (`rms_norm_composite`: `input.to(opmath_t)`; generated kernels accumulate the
statistic in fp32 registers), and upcasting a bf16-stored weight recovers no information.

At scale this is a significant delta. 

### Minimal reproduction

A single `Linear(4096, 4096)` followed by `RMSNorm(4096)`, model cast
to bf16, compiled, forward+backward under bf16 autocast, input (8, 4096, 4096). The only
difference between the two modes is whether the norm call is wrapped in
`torch.autocast(enabled=False)`:

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# ruff: noqa
"""Repro: rms_norm autocast fp32 policy materializes cast kernels under
torch.compile when input and weight are already bf16 (torch 2.12 vs 2.11).

Minimal setup: Linear -> RMSNorm, model cast to bf16, compiled,
forward+backward under bf16 autocast.

torch 2.11: rms_norm has no autocast registration; with matched bf16 dtypes
the compiled step emits no standalone copy kernels.
torch 2.12: rms_norm is registered under autocast's fp32 cast policy
(pytorch#174824), which promotes unconditionally; the promotion casts
materialize as standalone `triton_poi_fused__to_copy*` kernels and raise
peak memory.

Run (single GPU):
    python repro.py            # autocast-wrapped norm (regression path)
    python repro.py exempt     # norm under autocast(enabled=False) (workaround)
"""

import sys
import time

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

D, BATCH, SEQ, ITERS = 4096, 8, 4096, 20
EXEMPT = len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "exempt"


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(D, D, bias=False)
        self.norm = nn.RMSNorm(D, eps=1e-6)

    def forward(self, x):
        h = self.linear(x)
        if EXEMPT:
            with torch.autocast(x.device.type, enabled=False):
                return self.norm(h)
        return self.norm(h)


model = Net().to("cuda", torch.bfloat16)
model = torch.compile(model)


def step():
    x = torch.randn(BATCH, SEQ, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
    with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        out = model(x)
    out.float().sum().backward()


for _ in range(3):  # warmup + compile
    step()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

t0 = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(ITERS):
    step()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
step_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / ITERS * 1000
peak_gib = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 2**30

from torch.profiler import ProfilerActivity, profile

with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
    step()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

kernels = copies = 0
for ev in prof.key_averages():
    if getattr(ev, "device_time_total", 0) <= 0 or ev.key.startswith(("aten::", "Prof", "cuda")):
        continue
    kernels += ev.count
    if "to_copy" in ev.key or "convert_element_type" in ev.key:
        copies += ev.count

print(
    f"torch={torch.__version__} mode={'exempt' if EXEMPT else 'autocast'} "
    f"peak_gib={peak_gib:.2f} step_ms={step_ms:.2f} kernels/step={kernels} cast_kernels/step={copies}"
)
```

</details>

```bash
python repro.py            # autocast-wrapped norm (regression path)
python repro.py exempt     # norm under autocast(enabled=False) (workaround path)
```

Output on torch 2.12.1+cu130, single B200 (the LayerNorm line is the same script with
`nn.LayerNorm` substituted):

```
torch=2.12.1+cu130 RMSNorm   mode=autocast peak_gib=1.97 step_ms=7.01 kernels/step=15 cast_kernels/step=3
torch=2.12.1+cu130 RMSNorm   mode=exempt   peak_gib=1.47 step_ms=7.43 kernels/step=16 cast_kernels/step=0
torch=2.12.1+cu130 LayerNorm mode=autocast peak_gib=2.00 step_ms=7.67 kernels/step=19 cast_kernels/step=4
```

One norm costs +0.5 GiB peak (+34%): exactly one materialized fp32 copy of the (8, 4096, 4096)
bf16 activation (512 MiB), plus standalone cast kernels. The cost scales linearly with the number
of norm sites (see the at-scale numbers above). LayerNorm pays the same under autocast, confirming
the general Inductor behavior; for `rms_norm` this is new in 2.12 (no autocast registration on
2.11, where the two modes behave identically).

### Expected behavior
The `fp32` cast policy for `rms_norm` skips promotion when input and weight dtypes already
   match (the fused path dispatches fine and accumulates in fp32 internally)

### Workaround

Run the norm outside autocast; internal fp32 accumulation provides the same protection the policy
was adding externally:

```python
class AutocastExemptRMSNorm(nn.RMSNorm):
    def forward(self, x):
        with torch.autocast(x.device.type, enabled=False):
            return super().forward(x)
```

Measured at scale, this is faster and leaner than both the 2.12 default and the 2.11 baseline,
since the norm runs at bf16 I/O width on top of the improved 2.12 codegen.

comments.body: Does it make sense to move _(rms_norm) from AT_FORALL_FP32 (aten/src/ATen/autocast_mode.h L878 on main) to AT_FORALL_PROMOTE (L948). Matched dtypes should be safe to pass through, since the fused kernel already accumulates in fp32 internally and mixed dtypes are still promoted, so the #167308 fix should keep working. If yes, I can open a PR in the coming week.
